Ten Derby areas where the roof covering needs permission

Derby has sixteen conservation areas. In ten of them, Allestree, the Arboretum, Darley Abbey, Hartington Street, Highfield Cottages, Little Chester, Markeaton, Mickleover, Spondon and Strutts Park, an Article 4 direction means changing the roof covering on a slope that faces the road needs planning permission. The council’s FAQ puts doors and windows facing a highway under the same rule.

So if you’re in one of those ten and want to swap slate for something cheaper, check first. A like for like repair is a different matter from a change of material.

Source: Derby City Council, conservation areas, Conservation area FAQs (2016)

Slate, clay tile and chimney stacks in the guidance

The council’s guide to Little Chester and Strutt’s Park says blue-grey slate from north Wales and the Lake District was the usual roof there until the 1890s, and that concrete tiles and artificial slates aren’t acceptable substitutes. It rules out pantiles too.

Its Friar Gate appraisal describes the roofs as mainly slate and clay tile, and lists the removal of so-called redundant chimney stacks as a threat to the area. If a Derby stack needs work, repointing or rebuilding it is usually the route the council would rather see.

Source: Little Chester and Strutt’s Park guide, Friar Gate appraisal
